Sofia — quick lab summary and recommendation (pulled from recent bench runs):

Lab micro-benchmarks (representative numbers — 1x sequence = 68 tokens; 2x = 256 tokens):
- A100 (40GB) full GPU: TTFT@68 = ~135ms (P50), TTFT@256 = ~340ms; sustained tokens/sec ~220 at 50 concurrent streams when batched
- H100 (80GB) full GPU: TTFT@68 = ~95ms (P50), TTFT@256 = ~240ms; sustained tokens/sec ~360 at 50 concurrent streams
- L40S (48GB): TTFT@68 = ~145ms, TTFT@256 = ~380ms; sustained tokens/sec ~190
- MIG 2g slice (on H100): TTFT@68 = ~150-180ms depending on co-tenancy; best for predictable unit cost but worse tail latency

Notes:
- H100 full gives the best latency and throughput headroom — recommended for latency-sensitive interactive product (Acme's TTFT requirement).
- For cost-optimization, L40S or A100 with aggressive batching is viable for batch scoring workloads, but TTFT will not meet interactive goals without increased infra.
- MIG is useful if Acme wants denser packing with strict cost controls; recommend evaluating 2g slices for the 100-concurrency target as a secondary run.

Proposed prioritized run list for 2026-12-20 to 12-22 (parallel where possible):
1) H100 full — interactive profile (TTFT@68/256, concurrency sweep 1/10/50/100/300)
2) A100 full — same profile (to provide cost/latency delta)
3) L40S baseline — cost tradeoff checks
4) H100 MIG 2g — density/cost comparison (shorter run)

I'll attach the small CSV from last month's micro-run for reference. I'll also draft an estimated monthly delta (H100 vs A100) based on current on-demand pricing and the measured tokens/sec.

—Karthik
Applied ML / Performance
